title: One Icelandic Volcano Cancelled Over 100,000 Flights in 8 Days

scenes.text: One volcano in Iceland cancelled more than 100,000 flights.
In April 2010 it erupted and threw ash high into the sky over Europe.
Volcanic ash is tiny bits of rock and glass. It can wreck a jet engine.
So Europe shut its airspace. About ten million passengers couldn't fly.
It was the biggest air shutdown since the Second World War.
One eruption. Over one hundred thousand grounded flights.

description:
In April 2010 a volcano in Iceland cancelled more than 100,000 flights across Europe in eight days.
Eurocontrol counted about 104,000 cancelled flights and roughly 10 million passengers unable to board between 15 and 22 April. It was the largest airspace shutdown in Europe since the Second World War.
Were you stuck at an airport in 2010? Tell us below.
first_comment: A jet engine and volcanic ash do not mix. Where were you in April 2010?
